description: Linear algebra decomposed at depth. SVD applications, eigendecomposition + diagonalization, Jordan canonical form, Cholesky + LU + QR factorizations, conditioning, pseudoinverse, tensor algebra, Krylov subspaces, randomized linear algebra.

sub_mechanisms.name: SVD_geometric_interpretation
sub_mechanisms.definition: A maps sphere to ellipsoid. Singular values = semi-axis lengths. U, V rotate input + output.
sub_mechanisms.why: Foundation. Any linear map = rotation + scaling + rotation. Universal decomposition.

sub_mechanisms.name: low_rank_approximation
sub_mechanisms.definition: Best rank-k approximation via truncated SVD. Eckart-Young theorem.
sub_mechanisms.why: Foundation of PCA, image compression, recommender systems. Optimal in Frobenius norm.

sub_mechanisms.name: Jordan_canonical_form
sub_mechanisms.definition: Any complex matrix similar to Jordan blocks. Generalization of diagonalization.
sub_mechanisms.why: Handles non-diagonalizable matrices. Foundation of linear ODE theory. Standard result.

sub_mechanisms.name: Cholesky_decomposition
sub_mechanisms.definition: Symmetric positive definite A = LL^T. L lower triangular.
sub_mechanisms.why: Fastest factorization for SPD. Foundation of optimization (Newton method), kernel methods.

sub_mechanisms.name: QR_decomposition
sub_mechanisms.definition: A = QR. Q orthogonal, R upper triangular. From Gram-Schmidt or Householder.
sub_mechanisms.why: Foundation of least squares. Numerically stable. QR algorithm finds eigenvalues.

sub_mechanisms.name: condition_number
sub_mechanisms.definition: κ(A) = σ_max/σ_min. Measures sensitivity to perturbations.
sub_mechanisms.why: Foundation of numerical stability. Large κ: ill-conditioned. Standard analysis.

sub_mechanisms.name: Moore_Penrose_pseudoinverse
sub_mechanisms.definition: A^+ = VΣ^+U^T from SVD. Solves least squares.
sub_mechanisms.why: Foundation. Best least-squares solution to Ax = b. Used in regression, inverse problems.

sub_mechanisms.name: tensor_algebra
sub_mechanisms.definition: Multilinear algebra. Tensor product. Indices + Einstein summation.
sub_mechanisms.why: Foundation of general relativity, modern ML. Higher-order generalization of matrices.

sub_mechanisms.name: Krylov_subspace_methods
sub_mechanisms.definition: Span{b, Ab, A²b, ...}. Iterative methods for large sparse systems.
sub_mechanisms.why: Foundation. CG, GMRES, Lanczos. When direct methods too expensive (huge sparse matrices).

sub_mechanisms.name: randomized_linear_algebra
sub_mechanisms.definition: Use randomness for approximate but fast computations. Random projections.
sub_mechanisms.why: Modern. Johnson-Lindenstrauss. Approximate SVD via random sampling. ML at scale.

sub_mechanisms.name: matrix_calculus
sub_mechanisms.definition: Derivatives wrt matrices + vectors. ∂(x^T Ax)/∂x = (A + A^T)x.
sub_mechanisms.why: Foundation of ML optimization. Backprop calculations. Standard reference identities.

sub_mechanisms.name: spectral_theorem
sub_mechanisms.definition: Symmetric (Hermitian) matrices have real eigenvalues + orthonormal eigenvectors.
sub_mechanisms.why: Foundation. PCA = spectral decomposition of covariance. QM observables Hermitian.

derivation_rules.name: SVD_universal_tool
derivation_rules.why: Universal decomposition. Least squares, low rank, pseudoinverse, condition number all from SVD. Foundation of applied linear algebra.

derivation_rules.name: condition_number_predicts_numerical_problems
derivation_rules.why: Hilbert matrix: famously ill-conditioned. Standard diagnostic. Foundation of numerical analysis.

derivation_rules.name: Cholesky_fastest_for_SPD
derivation_rules.why: Half work of LU. Standard for Newton method, kernel methods, GP regression. SPD detection useful.

derivation_rules.name: spectral_theorem_simplifies_symmetric
then: orthonormal eigenbasis with real eigenvalues exists
derivation_rules.why: Foundation of PCA, QM. Diagonalization always possible. Standard simplification.

derivation_rules.name: randomized_methods_scale_to_huge_data
if: data is huge but low-rank structure expected
derivation_rules.why: Random projections preserve distances (J-L). Approximate SVD O(mn log k) instead of O(min(mn², m²n)).
